wave: SECURITY / SEMANTIC PRESERVATION -- FunctionIdentity, SymbolIdentity, StateAccessIdentity, and TypeIdentity all joined `scope.join()` (a bare, unescaped `::` concatenation of scope segments) directly into their identity_key() composite strings. A scope segment is not always a bare module-path identifier: `adapter::semantic::rust::handle_impl` pushes a segment like `"impl:Trait<Nested::Path> for Type"`, built from unrestricted type/trait spellings that can themselves contain `:`. FunctionIdentity additionally joined `generics` (via `,`) and FunctionOwner joined `trait_path` (via `|`) unescaped, both also fed by unrestricted `syn` token-stream spellings. TypeIdentity additionally joined its own `name` (a type spelling) unescaped via `|`.

After closing that single-dimension instance of this session's established unescaped-delimiter-join bug class, audited every other `identity_key()` in core/src/semantic for the same pattern by hand -- found it is far more widespread than one dimension: it is the CENTRAL identity for the three Exhaustive-coverage dimensions (FunctionIdentity, SymbolIdentity, TypeIdentity, per `adapter::semantic::rust::dimension_coverage`), not merely a Partial-coverage extraction dimension like OWNERSHIP. This is the highest-severity instance of the class found this session: a collision here silently merges two distinct functions/symbols/types into one identity, not just one observation site.
priority_classification: security / semantic preservation -- live defects (not verification gaps): all four collisions were independently constructed and confirmed to actually collide against the real, unfixed code before any change. Reachable from ordinary, advanced-but-non-adversarial real Rust source: an `impl` block for a nested-path/generic type, a generic bound like `T: From<(A, B)>`, or a const-generic array-length expression with `|` all produce free text that this codebase's own extractors already emit today.
gap_discovered_by: Self-directed continuation of generation 20's audit. After fixing OwnershipIdentity, manually read every remaining `identity_key()` in core/src/semantic/*.rs (function.rs, symbol.rs, state.rs, types.rs) for the same shape (a field joined via a literal separator with no `escape_identity_field` call), cross-referencing each free-text field's real producer in adapter/src/semantic/rust to confirm it is genuinely unrestricted before treating it as a defect rather than a false positive.
key_finding:
Four independent, confirmed collisions, all sharing the same root cause (`SemanticScope::join()` and several other fields have no escaping before being joined into an identity_key() string):
1. `core::semantic::mod::SemanticScope::join()` itself: two scopes with different segment lists (`["a::b", "c"]` vs `["a", "b::c"]`) render to the identical string `"a::b::c"` -- reachable because `adapter::semantic::rust::handle_impl` sets a scope segment to `format!("impl:{trait_path} for {self_type}")`, where `trait_path`/`self_type` are `path_spelling`/`type_spelling` output that can itself contain `::` (nested paths) or `|` (const-generic array-length expressions).
2. `FunctionIdentity::identity_key()`'s `generics.join(",")`: a generic bound's spelling (`generic_param_spelling`, via `syn`'s raw token-stream fallback) can contain a literal `,` (e.g. `T: From<(A, B)>`), confirmed to collide two different generics lists into one identity string.
3. `FunctionOwner::identity_key()`'s bare `trait_path` field, joined via `|`: `trait_path` is `path_spelling` output, which is not restricted to a bare identifier and can itself contain `|` via the same const-generic mechanism as (1).
4. `TypeIdentity::identity_key()`'s bare `name` field, joined via `|`: `name` is `type_spelling` output (the same unrestricted spelling class as (1)/(3)), confirmed to collide two different type identities into one string via a crafted `|`-containing name.
Each was independently constructed as a concrete byte-identical (or field-equivalent) collision and run against the real, unfixed implementation before any fix, per this session's own falsification discipline.
verification_before_acting: Read every identity_key() implementation in core/src/semantic/function.rs, symbol.rs, state.rs, types.rs directly, confirming each one joins `scope.join()` (and, for function.rs/types.rs, additional free-text fields) with no escaping.

Traced each suspect field to its real producer in adapter/src/semantic/rust: handle_impl (mod.rs) for scope segments, generic_param_spelling (spelling.rs) for generics, path_spelling (spelling.rs) for trait_path, type_spelling (spelling.rs, via TypeIdentity.name) for TypeIdentity -- confirming each is genuinely unrestricted token-stream text, not a bare `syn::Ident` (which the codebase already treats as safely `|`/`:`/`,`-free everywhere else, per `escape_identity_field`'s own doc comment).

Independently confirmed StateAccessIdentity.name and SymbolIdentity.name remain safe (built only from bare syn::Ident text via self_field_path/emit_symbol call sites, matching generation 20's sibling-dimension precedent) -- only `scope` needed fixing for those two structs, not `name`.

Constructed and ran a concrete collision for every fix BEFORE applying it: SemanticScope::join() (scope-level, generic across every caller), FunctionIdentity::identity_key() (both the scope vector and the generics vector, tested separately), TypeIdentity::identity_key() (the name vector). Each confirmed FAILED (collided) against the real, unfixed code first.

Re-ran cargo run -p atlas-cli -- systemize --root . against this repository's own real source tree after the fix, confirming coding_admission.blockers is still empty and the run completes cleanly -- no behavioral regression on this project's own real, non-adversarial corpus.

design_decisions.question: Fix `SemanticScope::join()` itself, or add a separate identity-safe method?
design_decisions.decision: Added a new `SemanticScope::identity_key()` method rather than changing `join()`'s own behavior. `join()` is also used for human-readable DISPLAY strings (`scoped_name()`, and the StateEntity graph node's display label) -- escaping it in place would corrupt those readable strings with backslashes for no benefit. `identity_key()` is a parallel, escaping variant used only where the result feeds a composite identity string.

design_decisions.question: How far to extend this generation's scope -- fix the whole class in one generation, or just SemanticScope and stop?
design_decisions.decision: Fixed every concrete instance found by direct inspection this generation (SemanticScope::join()'s four callers via the shared helper, plus FunctionIdentity's own generics field and FunctionOwner's trait_path field and TypeIdentity's own name field) -- each is the same root defect (an unrestricted syn token-stream spelling joined without escaping) and each was independently confirmed to actually collide, not merely suspected. Did NOT attempt a further exhaustive re-audit of every remaining struct in the codebase this generation (e.g. SymbolIdentity.name, which independent tracing already confirmed safe) -- that would be re-doing generation 20's already-thorough sweep rather than closing a newly found, higher-severity instance of the same class.

design_decisions.question: Did NOT touch the nested-composite-key embedding pattern (e.g. FunctionIdentity::identity_key() embedding `self.symbol.identity_key()`'s raw output as one field) -- is that also broken?
design_decisions.decision: Out of scope for this generation. That is a distinct, pre-existing architectural pattern used throughout the codebase (CallSiteIdentity, FunctionIdentity, every composite key that embeds a substruct's own identity_key()) that none of this session's prior escape_identity_field fixes have touched either. Fixing the LEAF free-text fields (what this generation does) is the established, narrowly-scoped fix class this session has consistently applied; redesigning the nested-embedding convention itself would be a much larger, unscoped architectural change outside today's finding.
